title: Remark
body_md:
Note that the sign of $f(x,y)$ is not specified in Definition \ref{Definition_Inhibition}.
Thus, when $y$ inhibits $x$, it may either slow the growth of $x$ or speed up its decay.

title: Example
body_md:
Let $\dot y=rx-y$, $r>0$ and consider the following general equations as possibilities for $\dot x = f(x,y)$:
\begin{eqnarray}
\dot x = f(x,y) &=& \frac{ax^n}{1+by} - cx\\
\dot x = f(x,y) &=& ax-by^n\\
\dot x = f(x,y) &=& \frac{ax^n}{1+by^m} - cx,
\end{eqnarray}
where $a,b,c>0$, $n,m\in \mathbb{Z}^+$ and $x,y \geq0$.
